known_facts_at_decision_date: Supertech Ltd. was a major real-estate developer with multiple large residential projects across India
Significant homebuyer delivery delays and project-completion failures had been reported across multiple projects
Union Bank of India had filed insolvency proceedings against Supertech
The default claim linked to the Eco Village II project exceeded ₹432 crore
Cash-flow mismatch between project collections and construction/delivery obligations was a central business problem
Homebuyer trust had deteriorated substantially due to repeated delivery failures
The company's financial position was under lender pressure from multiple creditors
Project-level ring-fencing of funds was a known governance concern in the sector context
Business priority was completion credibility, cash ring-fencing, lender and homebuyer coordination, and project-level resolution
Stalled projects created a spiral risk where inability to complete reduced future collections and further impaired cash flows
Project execution failure combined with debt pressure created an acute insolvency risk
